questions.stem: The Arjuna Award, given for outstanding performance in sports, was first instituted in which year?

options.option_text: 1956 — during the Melbourne Summer Olympics in Australia
1961 — instituted by the Government of India for sportspersons
1968 — following India's campaign at the Mexico City Olympics
1975 — when Indian hockey saw a revival in international play

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Arjuna Award was instituted in 1961 by the Government of India to recognise outstanding achievement in national sports. Option A (1956) is a common trap — India won hockey gold at Melbourne that year, but the award came five years later. The Dronacharya Award (coaches) and Dhyan Chand Award (lifetime) came even later.

questions.stem: The Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards recognise excellence in adventure sports. Which ministry of the Government of India confers these awards annually?

options.option_text: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India
Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
Ministry of Education, Government of India (formerly HRD Ministry)

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards are conferred by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports alongside the Arjuna, Dronacharya, and Khel Ratna awards. Option A (External Affairs) is a tempting error because Tenzing Norgay's Everest expedition was international in nature, but the award is entirely a domestic sports honour.

questions.stem: How does the 'Sahitya Akademi Fellowship' differ from the regular Sahitya Akademi Award?

options.option_text: It recognises only works originally composed in classical Sanskrit language
It is the Akademi's highest honour, conferred on 'immortals of literature'
It is awarded annually for the best debut novel in any Indian language
It is exclusively given for works translated into a foreign language

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Sahitya Akademi Fellowship is the apex honour of the Akademi, described as being given to 'immortals of literature' — only a small number of writers of towering distinction hold this at any time. The regular Sahitya Akademi Award (annual) is given for the best book in each of 24 recognised languages. Option C is wrong — the Fellowship has no 'debut novel' criterion whatsoever.

questions.stem: The Padma Awards — India's prestigious civilian honours — are officially announced on which occasion each year?

options.option_text: On the eve of Independence Day, i.e., on 14 August each year
On the eve of Republic Day, i.e., on 25 January each year
On Dr. B. R. Ambedkar's birth anniversary, i.e., 14 April
On the eve of Gandhi Jayanti, i.e., on 1 October each year

questions.explanation: B is correct. Padma Awards are announced on the eve of Republic Day (25 January); formal investiture ceremonies are held later at Rashtrapati Bhavan, typically in March–April. Option A is a classic confusion — in countries like the UK, honours are announced on the monarch's birthday or on the new year, but India ties Padma Awards to Republic Day, not Independence Day.

questions.stem: The National Film Awards of India, one of the most prestigious film honours, are presented by which authority?

options.option_text: Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), based in Pune, Maharashtra
Directorate of Film Festivals under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting
Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC), based in Mumbai, Maharashtra
National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), headquartered in New Delhi

questions.explanation: B is correct. The National Film Awards are administered by the Directorate of Film Festivals (DFF) under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Option C (CBFC) is the most tempting distractor as it is the most visible film-related body, but the CBFC only certifies films for public exhibition — it has no role in conferring awards. FTII trains film professionals; NFDC finances and distributes films.

questions.stem: The Booker Prize for fiction, one of the world's most prestigious literary awards, was originally known by a different name until 2002. What was its original name?

options.option_text: The Whitbread Prize for Fiction, awarded annually since 1971
The Booker McConnell Prize, named after its original corporate sponsor
The Commonwealth Writers' Prize for the Best Novel in English
The W.H. Smith Literary Award, given for outstanding prose fiction

questions.explanation: B is correct. The prize was called the 'Booker McConnell Prize' (1969–2002), named after its original sponsor Booker McConnell Ltd. In 2002 Man Group became the title sponsor and it became the 'Man Booker Prize'; from 2019 it reverted to simply 'The Booker Prize'. Option A (Whitbread) is wrong — the Whitbread Prize was a real but entirely separate UK literary award. Option C (Commonwealth Writers' Prize) was also a real independent award, now discontinued.

questions.stem: Which of the following facts about the Abel Prize in Mathematics is CORRECT?

options.option_text: It is given by the International Mathematical Union headquartered in Berlin
It is awarded by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, first given in 2003
It was instituted in 1895, the same year Alfred Nobel established his prizes
It is jointly administered by Princeton University and the Clay Mathematics Institute

questions.explanation: B is correct. The Abel Prize is awarded by the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters; it was established by the Norwegian government in 2001 and first conferred in 2003. It is named after Norwegian mathematician Niels Henrik Abel. Option C is a deliberate trap — Alfred Nobel's will was indeed signed in 1895, but the Abel Prize was created over a century later specifically to fill the absence of a Nobel Prize in Mathematics. Option D (Princeton/Clay) confuses it with the Clay Millennium Prize Problems.
